spec.intro: A plain text file holding one JSON object per line — one object per offer. Only the link is required; every other key is optional, and anything you leave out shows as “Not stated”.

fields.source_url: Link to the posting. It is what identifies the offer, so a line without one is skipped.
fields.title: The job title, worded as the posting words it.
fields.location: City, region or country the posting names.
fields.work_mode: One of remote, hybrid, onsite or unknown. Any other value is read as unknown.
fields.salary: Pay, written however the posting writes it — a range, an hourly rate or a single figure.
fields.contract_type: Form of employment, kept exactly as you write it.
fields.seniority: Experience level, for example Junior, Mid or Senior.
fields.required_skills: A list of strings. Each one becomes a requirement your CV is matched against.
fields.text: The full text of the posting. Keep it if you can: it is what Analyse reads to fill the remaining fields, and what lets a requirement be quoted later without opening the page again.
fields.collected_at: ISO 8601 timestamp of when you collected the offer. Without it, the moment of import is used.
fields.posted_at: ISO 8601 date the offer was published. Kept in the row’s note.
fields.board: Where the offer came from — a site name, or a label of your own. Kept in the row’s note.

spec.exampleNote: Written across several lines here so it can be read. In the file, each offer must sit on a single line.

rules.lines: One object per line: no enclosing array, and no commas between lines. Blank lines are ignored, and a line that is not valid JSON is skipped and counted back to you.
rules.extraKeys: Keys other than those above are ignored, so you can keep your own alongside these.
rules.duplicates: If the same link appears twice in one file, the last copy is the one kept.
rules.analysed: Company type and size, role profile, engagement length, ideal candidate, responsibilities, team and how to apply cannot be given as fields — Analyse fills them by reading text.
